legend: You are given an array A$$$A$$$ of length n$$$n$$$ and two integers M$$$M$$$ and K$$$K$$$. Determine if there exists a sequence P$$$P$$$ that is permutation of A$$$A$$$ such that for every consecutive pair, (pi+p2i+1)modM=K$$ \begin{aligned} (p_i + p_{i+1}^2) \bmod M = K \notag \end{aligned} $$ If a valid permutation exists, output any one; otherwise, output −1$$$-1$$$.
input: The first line contains three integers n$$$n$$$, M$$$M$$$, and K$$$K$$$, indicating the size of the array, the modulus, and the target value, respectively. The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$, representing the array A$$$A$$$.
output: If such a permutation exists, print 'YES' in the first line, followed by the permutation in the second line. Otherwise, print 'NO'.
